affectedPublicSurfaces: None on merge. The slice adds one transport module under apps/demo/src/lib/ and its unit tests. Nothing imports it: no route, page, layout, or bundle entry point references the helper, so the demo app's rendered surface and shipped assets are byte-identical before and after. The helper becomes reachable only when P-UI (W4-B) wires it into a view, which is a separate slice with its own release evidence.

candidateVerificationJourney.restrictedRoute: Local workspace tests on feature/issue-1132-fetch-streaming-client. No VPS is contacted and no deployment occurs.

journeys.name: fetch-streaming-transport-helper-unit
assertions: the helper uses fetch + ReadableStream and never constructs a native EventSource
the bearer token is sent in an Authorization header and never appears in a URL, query string, or log line
reconnect resumes from the last observed sequence number, so the caller sees no gap and no duplicate
401, 404 and 500 are distinguishable to the caller rather than collapsed into one opaque stream error
AbortController cancellation terminates the read loop without an unhandled rejection
the helper consumes the event union exported by packages/contracts and does not redeclare event shapes
no module under apps/demo imports the helper in this slice, so the built demo bundle is unchanged

htmlRoutes: No HTML route changes in this slice; the helper is unreferenced by any page.

migrationCompatibility.notes: No database migration and no public API schema change. The helper is a client of the SSE endpoint W3-B/P8-4 defines; it introduces no contract of its own. The event envelope it parses carries v: 1 and additive event types stay backward compatible by construction (ADR-074 d.2).

rollbackAssertion.preCutoverFailureBehavior: Do not merge. Nothing in the demo app depends on the helper, so not merging leaves the app exactly as it is today; P-UI simply has no transport to wire later.
rollbackAssertion.postCutoverFailureBehavior: Revert the commit. Because no module imports the helper, removing it cannot break a rendered surface, a route, or a build. The revert is a pure file deletion with no downstream reference to repair.

notes: Classified public-release because the slice writes into apps/demo/, which is a deployed surface, even though this particular change adds only an unreferenced module. The classification is treated as correct rather than worked around: the evidence below asserts the no-reference property instead of asserting that apps/ was untouched.
doNotInfer: Do not infer that a live run was streamed to a browser. That is W3-B/P8-9's HITL gate and needs a real Redis broker plus W3-A's runner merged.
Do not infer that the demo app's UI consumes agent events. P-UI (W4-B) owns the reducer and the staged run view; this slice ships transport only.
Do not infer that reconnect was exercised against a real network partition. The reconnect assertions are unit-level against a scripted stream, not an offline-toggle in a browser.
Do not infer that the SSE endpoint is deployed or reachable. The helper is written against the contract W3-B/P8-4 defines; no server is contacted during verification.
